tapeLine: Tuesday 27 October closed higher: S&P 500 +0.6% to 7,722.60, Nasdaq +1.18% to 26,477.81, Dow +0.03% (15.99 points) to 52,377.57, per CNBC and TheStreet coverage (27 Oct). Other outlets show S&P 7,722.52 and Dow 52,378.40. Wednesday futures were described as mixed to lower; no levels confirmed.
matters:
Chips led Tuesday: Broadcom rose about 4% after a bank group and Blackstone announced $63 billion of financing tied to Anthropic’s technology purchase, and Anthropic’s IPO filing kept lifting tech sentiment, per Yahoo Finance and CNBC coverage (27 Oct). SoFi closed up about 13.4% after beating Q3 estimates and raising guidance (Motley Fool, 27 Oct). Oil slid, per the same coverage.

The Fed announces its decision Wednesday 28 October and is widely expected to hold. Alphabet and Microsoft report after Wednesday’s close; Amazon is due later this week.

Invalidation triggered: the S&P 500 closed above Tuesday 20 October’s 7,712.57 close, which the prior brief named as the level that would reverse its read. It is now about 1.1% under its 7,811.54 record close of 9 October.
alsoOnTape: Gold, VIX and 10-year yield levels were not found with a clean dated source and are not carried.

secondOrder: Leadership narrowed: the Nasdaq gained 1.18% while the Dow was flat, so the index gains came from tech rather than broad participation. That is an observation, not a forecast.

The prior brief named the FOMC (27-28 October) and big-tech earnings as the scheduled catalysts; both remain ahead, with Tuesday’s move into them led by tech.
The 28 October FOMC decision has not yet been announced; a hold is expected.
